evidence.description: Traced the full Sprint-4 chain for staleness: REQ-23 explicitly consumes REQ-25's ratio-derived effective mode (not raw AUTONOMY) and reuses the REQ-21 shared module (grep-count==1 invariant, PROP-24) rather than reimplementing it; REQ-24's in-loop verify explicitly reuses REQ-22's independent-verify logic (not the publish tool's own stdout claim) and adds the UNCONFIRMED/no-blind-retry safeguard: no duplicate publish-click statement, no drifted terminology ('AUTONOMY variable' vs 'AUTONOMY flag' refer to the identical raw config value in both REQ-23 and REQ-25). REQ-20's Opus/main-agent browser-verify is explicitly scoped to the Mode-A trust ramp only ('once trusted, Mode B flips to autonomous publish... self-heal/self-improve removes the verifier too') and does not conflict with REQ-24's automated fetch-based V1 check, which operates at a different verification layer (publish-success confirmation, not content-quality judgment). No orphaned requirement, no requirement contradicted by a later one, no PROP left referencing a REQ number that doesn't exist.

Tier assignment is concrete and non-overlapping: T1 for 'config not hardcoded' (grep, no redeploy-required change), T2 for 'ratio consulted, correct, and fails closed on malformed input' (behavioral test proving N-1/1 split over N wakes AND all 4 boundary cases individually resolve to Mode A). The proof obligation is phrased as a binary, machine-checkable assertion set, not an aspiration -- each of the 4 malformed cases has an independently falsifiable pass/fail condition (assert effective_mode == A, assert no unhandled exception escapes, assert publish-call-count == 0).

The fail-closed mechanism is stated at the level of an implementation-agnostic invariant strong enough to falsify a naive `wake_count % N == 0` implementation directly: 'a div/mod-by-zero or parse error SHALL be caught and treated identically to "ratio says Mode A," not propagate as a crash or default to Mode B' -- this closes exactly the two failure classes (unhandled exception, and any except-path that silently defaults toward the MORE PERMISSIVE Mode B) that would have defeated Sprint 4's entire throttle-safety purpose (verification-architecture.md:78-80).

Re-verified PROP-24 (single-source publish-click statement + fault-injected non-reachability from Mode A) and PROP-25 (positively-tested success path + UNCONFIRMED-on-failure, no blind retry) remain internally consistent with the newly-tightened PROP-26 malformed-ratio requirement: a malformed ratio forces effective_mode=A, which is exactly the path PROP-24's dynamic call-count assertion independently proves never reaches the shared publish function -- the two proof obligations reinforce rather than duplicate or contradict each other.

summary: FIND-001 (iteration-9) is RESOLVED: REQ-25 and PROP-26 now require and name 4 distinct tested malformed-ratio boundary cases (missing/uninitialized, N=0, negative N, non-integer/otherwise-malformed N), each explicitly required to resolve to Mode A, never Mode B, never an uncaught crash -- closing the exact gap the prior round identified (a naive division/modulo implementation silently defaulting the safety throttle open). A full final pass across REQ-23/24/25 + PROP-24/25/26, cross-checked against REQ-2/6/7/20/21/22, found no remaining staleness, no drifted terminology, no orphaned or contradicted requirement, and no proof obligation left as a vague aspiration -- every SHALL in this range carries a binary, tier-assigned, machine-checkable test condition. The fail-closed direction is correctly biased toward the SAFE state (under-publish, never over-publish) in every malformed-input branch.
